name: Class 2
description: A throttle electric bicycle: the motor can propel it without pedaling, and stops helping at 20 mph, by throttle or by pedal assist. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low_speed_electric_bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
The motor may propel it on its own, with a throttle, but can't assist at all at 20 mph or faster
The motor disengages when the brakes are applied
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
A local authority may ban it from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
